messages.content: PNW got more concrete. Beaverton fair now ends 8:30 p.m.; Eugene breakfast moved to 7:45 a.m.; Seattle venue says load-in parking is limited. The Sunday afternoon Portland flight still works. Friday return is either a midafternoon Delta nonstop or a cheaper early flight. Car prices are all over the place by pickup and return hour. Can you rebuild the hotel sequence and tell me what to hold?

Yes. Quick check because it changes the late-drive math: is the Beaverton fair the night before the Eugene breakfast, and are the Friday choices roughly early morning versus about 1 p.m.? If so, I would rank this around sleep and airport buffer rather than lowest fare.
Correct. Tuesday fair in Beaverton, then Eugene Wednesday at 7:45. Friday is 7:05 a.m. on Alaska with a connection, about $160 cheaper, or a 1:10-ish Delta nonstop.

I would take the Delta nonstop and protect Friday. The early option means a predawn checkout, car return, bag drop, and a connection after a Seattle evening. For hotels: keep Sunday-Monday in Beaverton/Tigard, switch Tuesday to Albany rather than Salem or Eugene, then use Tukwila/Southcenter or SeaTac for Wednesday-Thursday. Albany is the best middle ground: less late driving than Eugene, much easier Wednesday morning than Salem. Main warning: Albany hotel breakfast may not open early enough to be useful before Eugene.
I’m leaning Albany. Is it still too late after the fair?

It is late but workable. If you leave the fair area by 8:45, Albany is roughly a 10:05-10:20 arrival depending on traffic and a quick stop. Eugene would push closer to 10:45-11:10, which is a lot after load-out. I would plan a real dinner before the fair or during the counselor meal, then keep the post-fair stop to gas, coffee, and maybe a packaged snack.
Salem is cheaper and shows breakfast included. Does that change it?

Only if the savings are meaningful and breakfast starts by 6:00. Salem gets you to bed a little earlier Tuesday, but Wednesday becomes tighter: depart around 6:05-6:15 for a 7:45 Eugene check-in. Albany lets you leave closer to 6:40. If Salem saves under about $60-$70, I would still choose Albany and bring a breakfast backup.
For Seattle, I don’t want to fight the airport on Friday. Tukwila/Southcenter or an airport hotel?

Tukwila/Southcenter is the cleaner base if the hotel has clear parking. It keeps you near SeaTac, gives you more walkable dinner options, and avoids being stuck with only hotel-market food. For the Seattle venue, assume parking is uncertain: arrive early for load-in, have the closest paid garage marked, and use rideshare only if the materials are light enough.
Car numbers: PDX pickup 4:15 Sunday and SeaTac return 11 Friday is $418. Returning after noon jumps to $560. Pickup at 6 p.m. is cheaper but awkward.

Keep the 4:15 pickup and the 11:00 return. The 6 p.m. pickup is not worth the hassle after landing, and the noon return risks a big price jump without helping much. Keep one car for the full loop; dropping and re-renting around Seattle would add more moving parts than it saves.
Can you give me the action list for tonight?

Tonight’s holds: 1) Flights: Sunday afternoon SLC-PDX and Friday 1:10-ish SEA-SLC nonstop; use the cheaper early flight only if finance rejects the fare gap. 2) Car: one-way PDX pickup Sunday about 4:15 p.m., SeaTac return Friday about 11:00 a.m.; confirm one-way fee, taxes, and mileage are included. 3) Hotels: Beaverton/Tigard Sunday-Monday with breakfast and parking verified; Albany Tuesday with late-arrival note and breakfast backup; Tukwila/Southcenter Wednesday-Thursday with free or clearly priced parking and dinner within walking distance. Also note: save a Tuesday dinner plan before load-out, do not count on Albany breakfast, and calendar the hotel cancellation deadlines before booking.

messages.content: I’m turning the PNW holds into reservations tonight. Chosen plan is open-jaw: Sunday afternoon SLC to Portland, Friday midafternoon Seattle to SLC, one one-way rental car PDX to SeaTac. Three hotel holds expire tonight: Beaverton, Albany, and either Tukwila or SeaTac. Walk me through the booking order before the rates roll.

Book in this order: flights first, then the one-way car, then hotels. Flights set the airport and timing; the car price is sensitive to return hour; the hotels are easiest to adjust if one detail moves. Before paying, screenshot the fare, car total with one-way fee, hotel cancellation terms, parking language, and breakfast times.
Flights are Delta Main Cabin: Sunday SLC-PDX 2:05 p.m. arriving about 3:10, Friday SEA-SLC 1:10 p.m. I can choose seats.

That is the right fare type for this trip. I would not use Basic because you need seat selection and schedule flexibility. Select window seats if available, and if one leg only offers preferred seats for a fee, skip the fee and set a reminder to check the seat map again after ticketing.
Car: compact is $421 with PDX pickup 4:15 Sunday and SeaTac return 11:00 Friday. Intermediate is $449. Noon return jumps to $560. I’ll have materials, but not a huge shipment.

Take the compact if the trunk will hold your suitcase plus materials; otherwise the intermediate is a reasonable $28 upgrade. Keep pickup at 4:15 and return at 11:00. Put your actual Friday target return closer to 10:15-10:30 so fuel, signage, and shuttle time do not eat the buffer.

Hotels: Beaverton queen room, breakfast 6:30, free parking, $169 for Sunday and Monday. Albany queen, free parking, breakfast 6:30, late arrival allowed, $142 Tuesday. SeaTac is $188 with $15 parking and shuttle but not much food. Tukwila is $196, free parking, breakfast at 6, restaurants next door.

Book Beaverton, Albany, and Tukwila. Tukwila wins over SeaTac once parking and dinner are included, and it still keeps Friday simple. Add a late-arrival note for Albany, request a quiet queen room if there is a notes field, and do not rely on the Albany 6:30 breakfast before Eugene.
Cancellation dates are Beaverton by Aug 19, Albany by Aug 20 at 6 p.m., and Tukwila by Aug 21. Any issue with that risk?

That risk is acceptable if the school schedule is now firm. Put calendar reminders 48 hours and 24 hours before each deadline. Tukwila is the most exposed because Seattle load-in details could change, so save one backup near SeaTac with a later cancellation window if you see one at a similar rate.
What dinner backups should I save in the itinerary?

Sunday/Monday: Beaverton or Tanasbourne area, easy after hotel check-in and after school visits. Tuesday: eat before the fair or during the counselor dinner, then keep a packaged snack for the Albany drive. Wednesday/Thursday: Southcenter restaurants near the Tukwila hotel. Friday: do not plan a sit-down meal before the airport; buy food after security.
Receipt list? My director will ask about the one-way car.

Save: itemized airfare receipt, seat-fee receipt only if any, rental confirmation showing PDX pickup and SeaTac return with one-way fee included, final rental agreement, fuel receipt, hotel confirmations, cancellation-policy screenshots, final hotel folios, parking receipts if any, and a short note that open-jaw plus one-way car avoids a late Portland backtrack after Seattle.
Great. Give me the final booking note I can paste into my file.

PNW recruitment loop booking note: Flights: Delta Main Cabin, Sunday SLC-PDX 2:05 p.m. arriving about 3:10 p.m.; Friday SEA-SLC 1:10 p.m.; window seats selected or requested where available, recheck after ticketing. Car: one-way rental, PDX pickup Sunday 4:15 p.m., SeaTac return Friday 11:00 a.m.; target actual return by 10:15-10:30; confirm one-way fee and taxes in total. Hotels: Beaverton queen room Sunday-Monday, breakfast 6:30, free parking, cancel by Aug 19; Albany queen Tuesday, late arrival noted, free parking, breakfast too tight for Eugene so bring backup, cancel by Aug 20 at 6 p.m.; Tukwila queen Wednesday-Thursday, breakfast at 6, free parking, restaurants nearby, cancel by Aug 21. Reimbursement rationale: open-jaw and one-way car reduce fatigue and protect the Friday return after the Seattle events.

messages.content: Ten days out and the PNW schedule tightened. First Portland school wants visitors there at 7:15 Monday. Beaverton added a counselor dinner before the fair, and the Seattle return flight moved 25 minutes earlier. Flights, car, and hotels are already booked.

Got it. What is the new Friday departure time, and are the hotels still Beaverton Sunday-Monday, Albany Tuesday, Tukwila Wednesday-Thursday? I want to protect the early school arrival and the SeaTac buffer.
Yes, same hotels. Friday SEA-SLC is now 12:45 p.m. Tuesday counselor dinner is 5, fair ends 8:30. Eugene breakfast is still 7:45 Wednesday.

Use this timing: Monday leave the Beaverton hotel by 6:35 for the 7:15 school arrival; hotel breakfast at 6:30 is too tight, so grab coffee only if it is ready and keep a bar or yogurt with you. Tuesday check out in the morning, keep the day bag separate, and plan to leave the fair by 8:45 for Albany. Wednesday leave Albany around 6:35-6:40 for Eugene.
Should I leave luggage in the car all Tuesday? I’ll have materials too.

Yes, but make it low-risk: suitcase and materials in the trunk before your first stop, laptop/ID/receipts with you, and do not open the trunk at the fair lot if you can avoid it. If the Beaverton hotel is close to your Tuesday route, ask them to hold the suitcase after checkout; otherwise the trunk plan is fine.
With the 5 p.m. counselor dinner, do I still need to plan dinner before the Albany drive?

Treat the counselor dinner as dinner if it is more than snacks. If it looks light, buy a sandwich before the floor opens and keep it in your bag. After 8:30, I would not plan a sit-down stop; just fuel, restroom, and go south.
And Friday with the 12:45 flight?

Friday: be checked out of Tukwila by 8:45-9:00, fuel before entering the airport loop, and aim to return the car by 9:45-10:00 even though the reservation says 11. That should put you at bag drop/security around 10:15. Breakfast at the hotel is fine if you are downstairs early, but do not let it push the car-return buffer.
